title: Console wayfinding: unified dashboard threads and workspace quick-paths
creator: Aisha Grant
description: Problem: Teams currently struggle to find the right path to monitor rollouts, inspect per-route cost breakdowns, and pivot between workspaces. Dense left-rail items + duplicated entry points have high cognitive cost. Goal: design a wayfinding system that surfaces coherent 'threads' — end-to-end journey entry points that group dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views — while preserving quick workspace switching and low visual noise. This ticket captures the prototype deliverable, evaluation feedback, and next steps for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype of 3 primary threads (Monitoring, Cost Ops, Rollouts) with annotated states
Clickable prototype demonstrating quick-switcher integration and persistent thread context
Usability test (n=8) with time-to-task and success metrics captured; >=80% task success for ‘view rollout impact on cost’
Design spec with accessibility contrast checks, keyboard navigation flows, and ARIA recommendations
Implementation-ready component list and tokens mapped to console design system
decisions: Adopt 'threads' as top-level discovery entry points instead of adding more left-rail links
Keep workspace quick-switcher as a persistent modal rather than embedding it in the left rail to reduce rail density
Expose per-thread breadcrumb and session-scoped context so users can switch workspaces without losing thread state
Prioritize keyboard-first accessibility for quick-switcher and thread traversal (Ctrl/Cmd+K entry + arrow navigation)
Defer multi-tenant role-aware custom threads to a follow-up ticket (post-MVP)
tradeoffs: Grouping flows into threads reduces discoverability of deeply nested features; mitigated via progressive disclosure and inline tooltips

Maintaining persistent thread state across workspace switches increases client-side complexity, requires session sync logic in the console; agreed to implement with an opt-in local state store then migrate to server-backed context if needed
Removing left-rail links reduces immediate access for power users; we will provide customizable pinning for advanced teams
prototype_notes: Prototype includes three threads: Monitoring (metrics, traces, alerts), Cost Ops (per-route cost, token breakdown, attribution), and Rollouts (canary config, traffic splits, auto-fallback)
Each thread presents a compact header with quick-actions (Open rollout, Open cost snapshot, Duplicate route) and a timeline micro-panel for recent changes
Thread cards are surfaced in the new 'Wayfinder' zone within the console home, prioritized by recent activity and SLO breaches
Hover states expose quick-links; click opens full thread view retaining breadcrumb context for workspace and model variant
accessibility_notes: Keyboard-only flows added for thread selection and quick-switcher interactions
Contrast ratios validated for thread cards and focus rings; tuned per WCAG AA
ARIA live region used for asynchronous rollout status updates to ensure screen reader visibility
metrics_and_success: Primary KPI: time-to-insight for 'determine cost impact of rollout' reduced by 40% in prototype tests
Secondary KPI: average left-rail click depth reduced by 1.2 clicks
Qualitative: 90% of testers reported lower cognitive load when completing cross-surface tasks
next_steps: Incorporate PM feedback on thread prioritization and add a 'pin thread' affordance (owner: PM)
Sync with ENG to validate session state complexity and propose API contract for thread context (owner: ENG)
Run extended usability in EU timezone and record additional accessibility sessions (owner: UX Research)
Prepare implementation ticket bundle with component specs, tokens, and interaction animations (owner: Design)
A/B test quick-switcher modal vs. embedded mini-switcher for power user efficiency (scope: 6 weeks)
